renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  id: junction_motif_bars
  title: Junctions by intron motif
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and each segment is the share of its splice junctions that carry one intron motif class. It answers whether the junctions look like real splicing.
    How to read: nearly all junctions should be the canonical GT/AG motif, with a small share of GC/AG and AT/AC. A large share of non-canonical junctions points to alignment noise or a damaged library, so check them against their read counts in the table.
    Lines and annotations: the motif classes fold the intron motif codes STAR writes in SJ.out.tab (0 non-canonical, 1 GT/AG and 2 CT/AC, 3 GC/AG and 4 CT/GC, 5 AT/AC and 6 GT/AT), joining each motif with its reverse strand reading. The folding is done by this catalog's recipe, and no cut-off is drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexdobin/STAR/master/doc/STARmanual.pdf
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: junctions_pct
    color: motif_class
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      junctions_pct: Junctions (%)
      motif_class: Intron motif

- component: card
  id: junctions_by_annotation
  title: Collapsed junctions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of collapsed splice junctions, and the bar shows the share that is annotated or novel. It answers how much of the splicing is known.
    How to read: a large annotated share is expected for a well-annotated organism. A large novel share points to unannotated isoforms or to alignment noise.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexdobin/STAR/master/doc/STARmanual.pdf
  column: junctions
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: annotation
  caption: junctions, by annotation

- component: card
  id: junction_reads_by_motif
  title: Reads crossing junctions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of uniquely mapped reads that cross a splice junction, and the ring splits them by intron motif. It answers where the spliced reads go.
    How to read: the GT/AG motif should hold almost all reads. The STAR manual advises removing non-canonical junctions supported by only a few reads as likely false positives, so a read-poor non-canonical slice is noise.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexdobin/STAR/master/doc/STARmanual.pdf
  column: unique_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: motif_class
  caption: reads, by intron motif

- component: table
  title: Splice junctions table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, an intron motif class and an annotation status, with the junctions and the uniquely and multi-mapping reads in it. It answers exactly how the junctions and reads divide up.
    How to read: filter to novel junctions and compare their reads per junction with the annotated ones.

- component: card
  id: unique_mapped
  title: Uniquely mapped reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of reads that STAR mapped to a single place, and the box shows the spread over samples. It answers how well the libraries align.
    How to read: a high median with a tight box is good. A low value or a long lower whisker marks samples to inspect in the read fate bars. STAR publishes no cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexdobin/STAR/master/doc/STARmanual.pdf
  column: uniquely_mapped_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: input_reads
  title: Input reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of input reads over all samples, and the histogram shows how many each sample has. It answers how deep the sequencing is and how even.
    How to read: samples far below the others have less power for expression or splicing analysis.
  column: input_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: total, with the per-sample range

- component: card
  id: multimapped
  title: Multi-mapped reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of reads that align to several loci, and the box shows the spread over samples. It answers how much of the library falls in repeats or paralogs.
    How to read: a sample with a much higher share than the others may be contaminated or rich in repeat or rRNA reads.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexdobin/STAR/master/doc/STARmanual.pdf
  column: multimapped_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: mismatch_rate
  title: Mismatch rate per base
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of aligned bases that differ from the reference, and the box shows the spread over samples. It answers how closely the reads match the genome.
    How to read: a high rate points to a divergent reference, variants, or sequencing errors. An outlier sample deserves a look at its quality report.
  column: mismatch_rate_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: annotated_splices
  title: Annotated splices
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of splices that match an annotated junction, and the box shows the spread over samples. It answers how much of the splicing matches the gene annotation.
    How to read: values near the top mean the annotation describes the library well. A low share suggests unannotated transcripts or a mismatched annotation.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexdobin/STAR/master/doc/STARmanual.pdf
  column: splices_annotated_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: unique_vs_mismatch
  title: Unique mapping against mismatch rate
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample: its mismatch rate on the horizontal axis and the share of uniquely mapped reads on the vertical axis, coloured by its multi-mapped share. It answers whether poorly aligned samples also carry more mismatches.
    How to read: good samples sit at the top left. A sample drifting to the bottom right has more errors and fewer clean alignments, so open it in the read fate bars.
    Note: STAR publishes no cut-off for either measure, so none is drawn. Few samples make a weak trend, and the table has the exact values.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median uniquely mapped read share of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of STAR.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    color_col: multimapped_pct
    x_title: Mismatch rate (% of bases)
    y_title: Uniquely mapped reads (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: mismatch_rate_pct
    y: uniquely_mapped_pct
    label: sample

- component: table
  title: Alignment summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its input reads, mapped, multi-mapped and unmapped shares, splice counts and error rates from the STAR final log. It answers exactly how each sample aligned.
    How to read: sort by uniquely mapped share to find the weakest libraries.

- component: figure
  id: read_fate_bars
  title: Where the reads went
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and each segment is the share of its input reads that STAR uniquely mapped, multi-mapped, mapped to too many loci or left unmapped, with the reason. It answers how well each library aligned and why reads were lost.
    How to read: a high uniquely mapped share is good. A large unmapped too short share points to adapter or quality problems, and a large too many mismatches share to contamination or a wrong reference. Compare with the summary table.
    Lines and annotations: the segments are STAR's own categories from Log.final.out and add up to the whole input. No cut-off is drawn because STAR publishes none.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexdobin/STAR/master/doc/STARmanual.pdf
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: reads_pct
    color: fate
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      reads_pct: Reads (%)
      fate: Read fate

- component: card
  id: read_fate_composition
  title: Reads by fate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of input reads, and the bar shows the share of each fate over all samples. It answers where the reads of the run end up.
    How to read: compare the uniquely mapped share with what is expected for the organism and library type, and open the bars to see which sample drags it down.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexdobin/STAR/master/doc/STARmanual.pdf
  column: reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: fate
  caption: reads, by fate

- component: table
  title: Read fate table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a read fate with its read count and its percentage of the input. It answers exactly how many reads fall in each fate.
    How to read: filter on a fate and sort by percentage to find the outlier samples.
